meta.description: Held-out GMPP pairs for ProjectLens narrative/date contradiction scoring. Not for tuning.
meta.yearConvention: prevYear/year use ProjectLens gmpp.json convention: year N = the release whose data is as at 31 Mar N (2020 = 2019-20 release, data as at 30 Sep 2019).

labelRules.contradiction: end date moved >14 days and the narrative says unchanged/the same, or names a current end date >14 days from the published one, without stating the actual move
labelRules.explained: end date moved >14 days and the narrative states the change
labelRules.no-move: published end date identical in both releases (daysMoved = 0)

meta.narrativeVerbatim: Narrative is the exact cell text from the current-year CSV (2019-20 and 2020-21 decoded as Windows-1252, others UTF-8), including line breaks, non-breaking spaces and any mojibake present in the source.
meta.licence: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.

cases.narrative:
Compared to financial year 19/20-Q2, the project's end-date remained scheduled to finish on 01 June  2026  . This is primarily due to the following factors: 

Schedule dates have been revised during contract negotiation contract signature in March 21.  Key milestones (50% confidence) are: 
- Initial Operating Capability (1 squadron of 18 tanks with crews trained at appropriate collective training standard) - November 27.
- Full Operating Capability (148 tanks delivered): November 30.

These dates are later than envisaged at Initial Gate.  This slip has arisen during contractual negotiations due to the perception in Industry of delivery and cost risk around the Design and Manufacture phases, reflecting that which has been witnessed from other projects.
cases.label: contradiction
cases.why: End date moved 791 days earlier (31 Jul 2028 -> 1 Jun 2026). The narrative says the end date 'remained scheduled to finish on 01 June 2026'. Its later text is about milestones (IOC, FOC) slipping later, not about the end date moving.
cases.doubt: The narrative does say 'Schedule dates have been revised', but it ties that to milestones moving later, while the end date moved earlier. A lenient reader might count that as stating the move.

The current forecast end date for the Programme is Q4 23/24 following the re-baselining in January 2024 as a result of significant delays to the design, build and test phase. The authority has been working closely with the suppliers to increase confidence in this revised delivery timeline. 

Despite the delays the Programme remains within the FBC approved spend envelope despite the delayed profile for benefits realisation.

cases.why: End date moved 176 days later (31 Jul 2024 -> 23 Jan 2025). The narrative names the current forecast end date as 'Q4 23/24' (by 31 Mar 2024). That is about 300 days before the published date, and earlier even than the previous one.
cases.doubt: It mentions 're-baselining in January 2024' because of delays, so it states that a change happened, but to a date that contradicts the column. 'Q4 23/24' may be a typo for Q4 24/25. Labelled 'contradiction' because the stated current end date is wrong by more than 14 days.

cases.narrative:
Compared to financial year 23/24-Q4, the project's end-date at 24/25-Q4 changed from 30/07/2024 to 30/06/2025. This is primarily due to the following factors; the original programme closure date was predicated on the associated legislation being in place in 2022.  The scheme regulations needed to remediate members did not come into force until 1 October 2023 which gave schemes 18 months to provide members with a choice i.e. 31 March 2025.
Following our IPA review in February 2024 it was agreed that the Programme should be extended to 30 June 2025 then move to a portfolio delivery for the remaining 4 projects
cases.label: contradiction
cases.why: The published end date moved 92 days earlier (30 Sep 2024 -> 30 Jun 2024). The narrative says it 'changed from 30/07/2024 to 30/06/2025' and was 'extended to 30 June 2025': a later date, 365 days after the published current date.
cases.doubt: Probably a year typo in the published End Date column. The narrative states a change, but in the opposite direction and to a different date. Labelled 'contradiction' because the narrative and the column disagree by a year.

cases.narrative:
Compared to financial year 23/24-Q4, the project's end-date at 24/25-Q4 increased from 31/03/2025 to 31/03/2026. This is primarily due to the following factors‚
The programme competed the development of the NUAR service and transitioned it to the appointed long-term operator by 31/03/25, within the approved schedule. Commitments to move to Public Beta by spring 2025, and to be fully operational by the end of 2025 remain on schedule.

The programme has received approval to extend by an additional 12 months to oversee the delivery of Public Beta and Fully Operational commitments, the progression of legislative measures, and to explore, through extensive stakeholder engagement and robust testing, if and how additional benefits could be delivered by increasing access to NUAR data.

This funding extension has, in part, been necessitated by fall of the Data Protection and Digital Identity Bill after the general election was called in May 2024. This meant a new Bill was required to pass the NUAR measures through parliament, extending timelines, which is required to full operationalise the service and fully realise the envisaged benefits.
cases.label: explained
cases.why: Moved 547 days later. The narrative states 'increased from 31/03/2025 to 31/03/2026' and that the programme 'has received approval to extend by an additional 12 months'. 'Remain on schedule' refers to Public Beta commitments.
cases.doubt: The 'from' date (31/03/2025) differs from the published previous date (30/09/2024); the new date matches.

  Unforeseen delays have been experienced when finding a temporary works solution for a listed structure and whilst mitigation measures have been implemented, the project completion date has changed by 15 weeks. The overall design and construction works are approximately 85% through the programme.
cases.label: no-move
cases.why: Published end date unchanged (18 Oct 2024). The narrative says it remained on that date but that 'the project completion date has changed by 15 weeks'.
cases.doubt: As above: the narrative states a change that the column does not show.
